data.narrative:
Ulysses Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $38M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable set spanning 9 private companies and 1 public equity in the same sector, including later-stage peers such as Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression methodology, using the $38M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yields $76M. Peer-median analysis across the four identified comparables produces a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B (10th percentile) to $2.0B (90th percentile).

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $65M to $2.0B, with a median of $888M. The wide range reflects a key tension: stage-progression anchors conservatively to deployed capital, while peer multiples assume Ulysses will achieve comparable scale and exit outcomes. The primary uncertainty is execution risk and whether the company's product-market fit and unit economics will support Series B valuations in line with Bedrock and Dexterity. Additional diligence on revenue, customer concentration, and technical differentiation would narrow this range materially.
